MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC WORKS COMMISSION AND PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
  JANUARY 20, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  PWC Chair Simmens called the meeting to order at 5:05 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Public Works Commission (PWC) Chair Lance Simmens; Vice Chair Wade
  Major; and Commissioners Scott Dittrich, Brian Merrick; and James Palmer (arrived at
  5:45 p.m.); and Public Safety Commission (PSC) Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug
  Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet, Keegan Gibbs, and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex
  Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ALSO PRESENT:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Susan Dueflas, Public Safety
  Manager; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public Works Director; Travis Hart, Public Works
  Superintendent; Arthur Aladjadjian, Public Works Superintendent; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Mary Linden, Executive Assistant; and
  Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  PSC Chair Frost led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  PSC Commissioner Gibbs moved and PWC Vice Chair Major seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 9-0, PWC
  Commissioner Palmer absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Senior Administrative Assistant Ayala reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  properly posted on January 14, 2022.

ITEM 1  NEW BUS1EESS

  A.  Westward Beach Improvements Project Update
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive an update on the Westward Beach
  Improvements Project; and 2) Provide a recommendation to City Council on any
  design modifications.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report. He provided a brief
  description of Measure M funding.

  Suzanne Guldimann stated this was the wrong project for 21st century due to sea
  level rise. She discussed the improbability of sand replenishment. She expressed
  concern about the lack of environmental studies. She stated she could not support
  the project.

  Philippe Browning stated he did not see a need for additional parking. He agreed
  with Ms. Guldimann regarding the vulnerability of the coastline. He stated the area
  was under water three times over the past year. He stated he appealed the project to
  the California Coastal Commission (CCC). He stated the funding would be better
  used elsewhere.

  Patt Healy, Malibu Coalition for Slow Growth, stated the project would not help
  Malibu residents. She stated Point Dume residents could support resurfacing the
  road, installing K-rail rather than the wall, and retaining existing parallel parking.

  Kraig Hill stated the site was adjacent to Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Areas
  (ESHA) on both ends and would be subject to appeal. He discussed sea level rise.
  He discussed the storm drain at Birdview Avenue on private property. He cautioned
  that a boardwalk must be biodegradable. He suggested repairing damaged asphalt,
  installing speed humps, and ensuring Birdview Avenue egress remains viable in the
  future. He suggested looking into a manufactured offshore reef. He expressed
  support for this to be a minimal project or leave it as it is.

  Jo Drummond stated the project should require a 100-year sea rise study and wave
  uprush study. She discussed community opposition to the project. She suggested
  additional studies on the effects on wildlife in the ocean. She agreed with Mr. Hill’s
  suggestion about constructing an offshore reef.

  John Mazza stated he was not speaking as a Planning Commissioner. He stated the
  City Attorney had advised the Planning Commission that it could make no changes.
  He stated CCC would be releasing a new wave uprush study in the next few weeks.
  He stated that study will be required. He asked about traffic impacts of the new
  hotel and questioned whether 35 parking spaces were worth the cost. He discussed
  loss of sand during the 1983 storms. He stated the sand wall would not have been
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission

  approved by CCC. He suggested the funds would produce better reward value in
  other areas.

  PSC Chair Frost stated pedestrian safety was critical. He suggested keeping the
  project away from the sand and within the right-of-way. He discussed impacts of
  valet parking at the restaurant. He stated the parking was designed to not allow for
  parking of motorhomes and trailers.

  PWC Commissioner Dittrich presented photographs of the project area. He stated
  the erosion displayed was beyond the scope of this project. He agreed with PSC
  Chair Frost that cars going to the restaurant should not be allowed to stop in the
  roadway. He discussed use of parking spots by the restaurant. He agreed with
  installing a wooden walkway. He suggested parking meters be considered. He
  stated angled parking would help keep out recreational vehicles (RVs). He stated
  the project did not impact the ocean or sea life. He disagreed with installing a reef
  at Westward Beach due to its negative impact on the break.

  PSC Commissioner Gibbs stated he looked at this project from primarily a public
  safety perspective. In response to PSC Commissioner Gibbs, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated the project was not in response to a CCC request for additional
  parking. He explained it originated with the Public Works Commission. PSC
  Commissioner Gibbs asked for pedestrian versus auto accident statistics. He stated
  he agreed with the safety aspects of the project. He questioned the environmental
  impact, particularly related to sea level rise. He stated widening the road would
  result in structural issues in the future.

  PWC Commissioner Palmer arrived at 5:45 p.m.

  PWC Vice Chair Major thanked the speakers and those who submitted comments.
  He stated safety had to be first and the beach second. He stated a sea wall was a
  non-starter. He stated parking had to be reduced overall and current parking
  accommodated more cars than necessary for visitors to Westward Beach. He
  suggested a 100-year sea rise study. He agreed with investigating the storm drain
  at Birdview Avenue and providing non-intrusive signage that indicated available
  parking. He stated the project should not include any wooden structure due to fire
  risk. He agreed with considering blinking lights. He asked if there could be no left
  turn from PCH. He disagreed with adding parking meters. He stated RVs should be
  restricted. He stated not enough people were aware of this project when it was first
  proposed. He requested better noticing of projects in the City.

  PWC Commissioner Merrick discussed the original reasons for this project. He
  agreed with speed humps and parking availability signage that would also direct
  vehicles to the Zuma lot. He disagreed with PWC Vice Chair Major that the parking
  lot at Point Dume State Beach often filled up leading people to this lot. He disagreed
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission

  with diagonal parking and any road easement. He suggested fixing the shoulder and
  keeping the bike path and parallel parking. He suggested looking into
  improvements on the inland side of the road. He agreed with PSC Chair Frost that
  the restaurant valet parking was a major issue. He suggested closing the road when
  the lot was full and redirecting vehicles to Zuma Beach. He disagreed with
  scrapping the project because gridlock and pedestrian safety needed to be
  addressed.

  PSC Vice Chair Stewart stated the community thinks this is a critical issue. He
  stated the project should stay within the easement or right-of-way. He stated the
  road was a major artery for Point Dume in an emergency. He discussed illegal
  parking when the lot was full. He agreed with installing signage to indicate parking
  availability. He stated pedestrians needed to be kept out of the street. He stated
  parallel parking was ideal. He stated any sidewalk should be minimal and have a
  curb. He stated open car doors should be addressed in the design. He stated the
  current design would not survive rising tides. He proposed minimizing the project
  to only within the City’s right-of-way, including a striped walkway that would
  allow for opening car doors, minimize parking, stripe parking spaces to restrict
  oversized vehicles and enforce it, keep cars off the street if there is no parking.

  PWC Commissioner Palmer suggested looking at a short-term solution and
  redesigning the project to preserve the road from erosion.

  PSC Commissioner Spiegel agreed the project should be kept within the right-of-
  way, the restaurant be required to correct issues, weddings be disallowed, and the
  road closed if the parking lot was full. He stated he discussed beach restoration with
  Tom Ford, Bay Foundation, who agreed something could be done. He suggested
  the recommendation to the Council include working with Bay Foundation on dune
  or beach restoration.

  PSC Commissioner Anneet discussed the letters received from many members of
  the community. He stated residents will stand up for Malibu’s treasured beaches.
  She stated research and studies needed to be conducted and clearly state what any
  project is trying to solve. She stated more parking spaces added to the public safety
  problem. She discussed pedestrian safety issues on Birdview Avenue. She stated
  focus should be on minimizing and safely directing traffic, expanding parking on
  the other side of the road, reducing traffic flow and ensuring traffic flow safety on
  busy weekends, restricting RVs, providing safe passage from the other side of the
  road, and minimizing impacts on beach sand.

  PWC Chair Simmens stated there were solid, positive elements of the project that
  could be retained while balancing public safety and environmental concerns.

  PWC Commissioner Dittrich suggested putting parking availability signage on the
  road before vehicles entered the area. In response to PWC Commissioner Dittrich,
  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the City’s oversize vehicle ordinance could
  restrict RVs from parking in the lot. He stated striped parking spaces or a parking
  kiosk could restrict RVs. He stated the City’s ordinance required that vehicles be
  parked within the lines of a striped parking space.

  Public Works Director DuBoux acknowledged that most Commissioners did not
  support angled parking and did support staying within the City’s existing right-of-
  way. He asked for Commission input regarding a pedestrian walkway. He stated
  the walkway made this project eligible for the Measure M funding that had been
  used for project design. He stated removal of the walkway would require the City
  to reimburse Metro for funds used. He asked for input about the suggested width of
  a walkway. He stated a sea level rise study could be included in any redesign.

  PWC Chair Simmens stated it seemed the Commissioners did not support the sand
  wall. He asked if another material could be used for a walkway. Public Works
  Director DuBoux discussed raised walkways installed by other beach communities.
  He stated a resin material could be used.

  PSC Commissioner Gibbs stated a walkway on the beach side of the parking lot
  was not necessary. He stated the current width of the older road was a good
  potential, along with a bike path.

  PSC Chair Frost stated the oversized vehicle ordinance was only effective during
  night hours. He suggested striping and signage indicate parking was for passenger
  vehicles only. He disagreed with PSC Commissioner Gibbs that a walkway on the
  beach side would keep people off the road. He agreed with PWC Commissioner
  Merrick and PWC Chair Simmens that this project did not need to be scrapped. He
  stated he did not think CCC would allow parking meters.

  In response to PWC Commissioner Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  the current parallel parking and the walkway could be accommodated within the
  right-of-way. In response to PWC Commissioner Dittrich, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated installing a sign to indicate parking availability would have to be
  done in conjunction with the County.

  In response to PSC Vice Chair Stewart, Public Works Director DuBoux clarified
  what could be built within the City’s right-of-way. He explained the dimensions for
  parallel parking. He stated the travel lanes were currently 12 feet and 14 feet on the
  beach side. He stated 12-foot lanes on both sides could be accommodated along
  with 11-foot wide parallel parking with at least 15 feet for a walkway. PSC Vice
  Chair Stewart agreed with the walkway being installed on the beach side and
  keeping bicycles off the roads. He disagreed with using resin for the walkway.

MOTION  PWC Commissioner Merrick moved, and PWC Commissioner Dittrich seconded a
  motion to recommend that staff bring back an item to the Public Safety Commission
  and Public Works Commission with redesign options for the Westward Beach
  Improvements Project bringing forward an improvement plan to Westward Beach
  Road that includes but is not limited to signage, pedestrian safety, speed humps,
  bicycle and traffic control, with no walls or head-in parking, to be placed within the
  current City right-of-way and including both sides of the road.

  PSC Commissioner Spiegel suggested adding language to ask the City to work with
  the Bay Foundation on beach restoration.

  Public Works Director DuBoux suggested he could include reaching out to the Bay
  Foundation, particularly about dune restoration, in the Work Plan.

  PWC Commissioner Merrick stated he could not support including Public Safety
  Commission Commissioner Spiegel’s suggestion in the motion at this time but was
  open to discussing it later.

  PSC Commissioner Anneet stated it was important that any redesign not intrude on
  the beach and include appropriate studies.

  PWC Vice Chair Major agreed with PSC Commissioner Anneet.

  PSC Commissioner Spiegel noted that the project was located in a marine reserve.

  PSC Vice Chair Stewart suggested a reasonable amount of time be given for
  reconsidering this item. Public Works Director DuBoux stated timing for finding
  and availability of the consultant needed to be considered. He said it would be
  brought back as quickly as possible.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  PWC Chair Simmens thanked the Commissioners for their patience and input.

  B.  Los Angeles County Measure R and M Transportation Funding Projects
  Recommended Action: 1) Identify projects to improve safety on Pacific Coast
  Highway and canyon roads using Los Angeles County Measure R and Measure M
  transportation funds; and 2) Provide a recommendation to City Council.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report. He explained differences in
  requirements for Measure R versus Measure M funding. He stated all Measure M
  projects and some Measure R projects were identified in the City’s PCH Safety
  Study, which has been used to prioritize projects. He stated staff was considering
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of January 20, 2022
Page 7 of 8

  contacting State representatives to identify additional State funding available so
  Measure R and Measure M funds were not necessary. He discussed the lengthy
  Metro process for funding approval. He stated a local cycling advocate had
  contacted him about the need for safety improvements on PCH between Santa
  Monica and Cross Creek Road. He stated the advocate’s suggestions, primarily to
  provide space between bicycles and cars, were included with the staff report.

  PWC Chair Simmens stated Caltrans needed to create a cycling green zone on 80%
  of PCH, at least westbound.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated cycling safety was a priority for the PCH
  Task Force.

  PSC Vice Chair Stewart stated the Las Flores Canyon area was the highest priority
  for the Public Safety Commission. He stated Webb Way, the Civic Center area, and
  Big Rock were other high traffic accident areas. He stated evacuation plans and
  traffic signal coordination were critical.

  PWC Commissioner Dittrich stated agreed with PSC Vice Chair Stewart about
  evacuation concerns, and that Big Rock, Las Flores and Rambla areas needed
  attention. He discussed the limited width of the highway in eastern Malibu. He
  asked if a public safety pilot project to eliminate above-ground power poles could
  be included.

  PSC Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated the Public Safety Commission agreed
  with prioritizing projects based on historical accident and fatality data. He agreed
  with working with Caltrans to expedite safety projects. He stated evacuations
  should be considered in any recommended projects.

  In response to Public Safety Commission Chair Frost, Public Works Director
  DuBoux suggested using the PCH Safety Study for identifying priorities. PSC
  Chair Frost stated the Las Flores Canyon intersection should be the top priority.
  RDB stated synchronizing signals from Trancas Canyon to Paradise Cove could be
  moved down.

  Public Works Director DuBoux requested the Commissions identify the top
  priorities. He stated staff would bring back the updated list at another Joint Special
  meeting.

  PWC Vice Chair Major discussed the issue of transients and homelessness in
  increased traffic accidents and fatalities. He stated improvements related to that
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of January 20, 2022
Page 8 of 8

  problem would change PCH safety.

MOTION  PSC Chair Frost moved, and PWC Commissioner Dittrich seconded a motion to
  continue the item to another Joint Special meeting of the Public Safety Commission
  and Public Works Commission. The question was called, and the motion carried 9-
  0, PSC Commissioner Gibbs absent.

  PSSC Chair Frost thanked Public Works staff.

  PSC Vice Chair Stewart suggested putting in priority tiers.

  7:34 sim adjourned the meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

  At 7:34 p.m., Public Works Commission Chair Simmens adjourned the meeting.

  Approved and adopted by the Public Works Commission of the City
  of Malibu on February 23, 2022.

  ~NC  MENS, Chair
